items.headline: Rahul Gandhi accuses Centre of police brutality against NEET protesters; Rijiju hits back
items.summary: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi attacked the government over police brutality during NEET protests, while Union Minister Kiren Rijiju defended the Delhi Police and cited Congress-era police actions.

items.headline: Jharkhand competitive-exam protests called off after Soren government cancels JSSC CGL exam
items.summary: After 26 days of agitation, Jharkhand's competitive-exam protests ended when the Hemant Soren government cancelled the JSSC CGL exam; a separate PGT recruitment protest continues.

items.headline: Bombay High Court cancels bail for Goa Birch nightclub owners in fire that killed 25
items.summary: The Bombay High Court cancelled bail for the Luthra brothers, owners of Goa's Birch nightclub, over a fire that killed 25 people amid a lack of safety measures.

items.headline: US envoy Sergio Gor says Washington may re-evaluate its travel advisory for Kashmir
items.summary: US Ambassador Sergio Gor said Washington may re-evaluate its Kashmir travel advisory, citing improved safety, after meeting J&K CM Omar Abdullah in Srinagar.

items.headline: Chennai MRTS to merge with Metro Rail after 15 years, changing fares and services
items.summary: Chennai's MRTS network will be integrated with Chennai Metro Rail after 15 years, a merger set to change fares, ticketing and services for daily passengers.

items.headline: US sanctions ICC president and a senior prosecutor in escalating campaign against the court
items.summary: The Trump administration sanctioned ICC President Tomoko Akane and senior lawyer Abdoulaye Seye, bringing to nine the number of the court's 18 judges sanctioned.

items.headline: Israeli airstrikes hit a Syrian air base hours after a Turkish delegation's visit
items.summary: Israel struck the runway of the Abu Duhur air base in Idlib, saying it aimed to stop Turkish troops deploying there; Turkey and US envoy Tom Barrack condemned the strikes.

items.headline: Trump pauses threatened 50% tariffs on Canada as a trade deal remains unfinished
items.summary: Trump delayed a threatened 50% tariff on Canadian goods after talks with PM Mark Carney, who said the pause runs until August 22; key terms remain unsettled.

items.headline: Congo's Ebola outbreak reaches 5,000 cases as the response falls behind
items.summary: Congo's Ebola outbreak, caused by the Bundibugyo virus in Ituri province, has reached 5,000 cases and over 2,300 deaths, spreading about three times faster than the 2014-2016 epidemic.

items.headline: Central African Republic gold mine collapse kills more than 100 people
items.summary: The death toll from the collapse of an artisanal gold mine in Zamboye, near the Cameroon border, rose above 100, with others still missing; authorities opened an inquiry.

items.headline: IDFC First Bank raises $500 million in its maiden overseas bond issue from GIFT City
items.summary: IDFC First Bank sold $500 million of three-year senior notes at a 5.625% coupon via its GIFT City IFSC unit, drawing BlackRock, Capital Group and AllianceBernstein.

items.headline: India set to see up to $1.5 trillion in family wealth change hands over the next decade
items.summary: A Julius Baer-EY report estimates $1.3-1.5 trillion of Indian family wealth will transfer between generations over ten years, expanding family offices and alternative investments.

items.headline: Escorts Kubota to invest Rs 2,000 crore in a new tractor and equipment plant in UP
items.summary: Escorts Kubota announced a Rs 2,000 crore plant across 154 acres in YEIDA, Uttar Pradesh, set to be one of the Kubota Group's largest global facilities.

items.headline: Gold slips on MCX to nearly Rs 1.54 lakh per 10 grams as US Treasury yields ease
items.summary: MCX October gold futures fell Rs 133 to Rs 1,54,129 per 10 grams as US Treasury yields cooled ahead of the Fed minutes; spot gold edged up 0.2% to $4,342 an ounce.

items.headline: SEBI impounds Rs 3.67 crore and bars two entities over Sensex expiry-day manipulation
items.summary: SEBI passed an interim order against Copthall Mauritius Investment and Mansi Share and Stock Broking for manipulative trades on a Sensex weekly-expiry day, impounding Rs 3.67 crore.

items.headline: Telescope clocks the fastest star yet seen orbiting the Milky Way's black hole
items.summary: Astronomers using the ESO Very Large Telescope found a star circling the Milky Way's central black hole at about 25,000 km/s, completing an orbit every 8.7 years; published in Nature.

items.headline: China recovers a rocket's first stage on land for the first time
items.summary: Xinhua said LandSpace's reusable Zhuque-3 rocket launched Wednesday and its first stage touched down on landing legs, China's first land recovery of a booster.

items.headline: NASA orbiter captures the sharpest images of a crater left by a crashed rocket on the Moon
items.summary: NASA's Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter released photos of the ~60-foot-wide crater gouged when a Falcon upper stage struck the Moon at about 5,400 mph on Aug. 5.

items.headline: Archaeologists unearth a sacrificial burial by Lima's ancient Huaca Pucllana pyramid
items.summary: In Lima, a team led by archaeologist Gladys Paz unveiled the skeleton of an adult man believed sacrificed when a ceremonial canal was ritually closed at the Huaca Pucllana pyramid.

items.headline: Personalized mRNA cancer vaccine keeps melanoma at bay longer in a trial
items.summary: Moderna and Merck said their tailored mRNA vaccine intismeran, with the immunotherapy Keytruda, kept melanoma patients free of recurrence or spread longer than Keytruda alone.

fun_fact.headline: The Eiffel Tower grows about 15 cm taller in summer
fun_fact.body: The Eiffel Tower is taller in summer than in winter. Iron expands as it warms, so on a hot day the sun-heated tower can stand about 15 centimetres taller than on a cold winter day. The effect is deliberate: its engineers designed the wrought-iron structure to flex with the seasons rather than crack.

puzzle.title: The Reunion Handshakes
puzzle.body:
Everyone at a reunion shook hands with each other guest exactly once. Altogether there were 78 handshakes.

(a) How many guests were at the reunion?
(b) If three more guests had arrived — each also shaking hands once with everyone present — how many handshakes would there have been in total?
puzzle.approach: Each of n guests shakes n−1 hands, but that counts every handshake from both sides.
puzzle.answer:
(a) 13 guests. With n guests the number of handshakes is n(n−1)/2. Setting n(n−1)/2 = 78 gives n(n−1) = 156 = 13 × 12, so n = 13.

(b) 120 handshakes. With 13 + 3 = 16 guests present, the total is 16 × 15 / 2 = 120.

word_puzzle.title: Sound Check
word_puzzle.body:
Unscramble each into a single word, then say what the four have in common:

1.  OILVIN
2.  MURD
3.  PET RUMT
4.  RATGIU
word_puzzle.approach: Unscramble each cluster into one word. Once you have all four, name the category they share.
word_puzzle.answer:
1. VIOLIN
2. DRUM
3. TRUMPET
4. GUITAR

The hidden link: all four are musical instruments.
